issues.detail: The Hebrew 'בֶּן שְׁנָתוֹ' means 'a year old' (literally 'son of its year'), but the Vietnamese says 'giáp năm' which means 'one year old' — this is correct. However, the Vietnamese adds 'đực' (male) which is not in the Hebrew; the Hebrew only says 'כֶּבֶשׂ' (lamb) without specifying gender. This is an addition that changes the meaning.
